The annotation guide defines these four tags as standalone: when one is applied, no other tag or object label applies to that picture. The annotations were checked against this rule and no exceptions were found. The fourth class appears under two spellings in the files (P2_FOV and F2_FOV); both are counted here.
Both show the area of interest cut off. Off-centre image with the package correctly seated = Cavity Off Center; package not seated or out of position = Primary Package Misalignment.
Both look like the lens has moved. If the cause is too little solution, it is Low Dose; a real shift in a well-filled bowl is Lens Off Center.
Wet package marks look like bubbles but are liquid: gradual brightness change, irregular outline, usually near the package edge.
Mixed shapes (a strand with a clump) are recorded as Fiber; Extraneous Polymer only when the material is clearly polymer.
A groove that opens into a tear or flap is Torn Lens; a shallow surface channel is Surface Groove.
Raised or extra material is Extraneous Polymer; a groove is missing material.
Torn lens stays in one piece; rupture separates it into pieces.
Edge deformation with a continuous edge is Edge Bottle-Capped; a tear into the lens is Torn Lens; separated material is Lens Rupture.
Scatter is a whole-picture tag for many small bubbles spread widely; single bubbles and touching groups are marked objects.
Same kind of contamination, different focus: strobe marks are soft and creep in from the edge; camera marks are sharp anywhere in the picture.
No Lens requires a valid package and confidence that no lens is present; otherwise the specific condition applies.
Not a conflict: a folded lens in a multi-lens picture carries both tags.
Anything that cannot be confidently called a bubble is recorded as the most appropriate foreign-matter class.
Uncertain features are recorded under the closest class; consistency is preferred over guessing the physical cause.

The width and height of the outlined object in image pixels. Sizes describe the object, not its rotation.

The three picture sets in this workbook are nested. The earlier count looked at every annotation file; the analysed set applies the current rules; the training/test set also drops classes that are no longer used.
Why class rows do not add up to the totals

A picture can carry more than one tag, or several marked objects. Class rows therefore count class memberships: 4,568 training pictures carry 6,268 class memberships. The training and test totals count each picture once, so they are smaller than the column sums. Marked objects are the exception: each object belongs to one class, so that column does add up to its total.
